decisions.reason: The approved Hero V remains the unchanged reference geometry; the source modifies only how its characteristic reach is carried into the lowercase v.

The candidate already requires the É accent to be the literal intact terminal section of the approved Hero V. The exact-overlay language reiterates that existing rule, while the construction diagram is optional.

The existing state already requires one unified terminal gesture across the Hero V, second V, and É accent. The new restrained lowercase reach concerns the second V's arm extension, not a change to the shared terminal treatment.
The source applies the existing proprietary identity goal to two specific letterform details but does not change the broader brand expression requirements.
The source addresses letterform geometry and contains no change to material treatment, finish, or the deferred design sequence.
The source refines the lowercase v and É accent within the V system but neither resumes nor changes the deferred construction of the remaining proprietary wordmark letterforms.
Mention that the lowercase v should sit as part of the architectural system does not alter the deferred wordmark composition, kerning, rhythm, or hierarchy requirements.
The source refines internal V-system geometry without changing the decision to use a wordmark-led identity without a separate icon or monogram.
